decisions.reason: The source grants placement flexibility for the integrated one-board variant; this candidate governs connector placement only for the separate three-board variant.
The integrated-board variant was already established, and the source does not remove the separate-board variant or otherwise change the recorded architecture attributes.
General placement flexibility remains subject to the antenna direction and keepout constraints established in message 842.
This candidate concerns the separate power board's form factor and connector access; the source addresses placement on the integrated-board variant.
The source concerns general connector positioning and does not change pin coverage, breakout format, hole placement, platform purpose, or the unresolved pitch conflict.

The source states that the current design has one board, while the enclosure state accommodates and mounts three boards; it is unclear whether that task-local enclosure must be redesigned for the integrated variant or remains specific to the separate-board design.
The source addresses placement flexibility on the integrated board and does not change the separate sensor board's requirement to fit all required content.
The candidate records dimensions and routability for the separate main board; the source concerns connector placement on the integrated-board variant.
Connector placement flexibility on the integrated board does not alter the separate power board's layer count or ground-plane strategy.
The interboard power interface is explicitly scoped to the three-board variant; the source discusses the integrated variant and does not remove or modify the three-board interface.
The source changes physical placement flexibility only and does not change component availability, alternative sourcing, cost, or assembly policy.
Allowing flexible connector positions does not change the requirement that integrated-board connectors use through-hole mounting.
